messages:
alex.support: heads up — customer reported truncated stream when their client reconnects mid-response. they see the main body but the final JSON object is incomplete and there is no finish_reason. they tried Last-Event-ID reconnection and ended up with duplicate partial payloads. attaching their repro logs below.

maria-engineer: thanks alex. can you paste the exact curl or client snippet they used? also which SDK and network environment (browser/node/proxy)?

alex.support: they sent this minimal repro (browser -> corporate proxy -> our edge):

```\n// client: browser fetch SSE-like using EventSource polyfill
const es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?model=redwood-large', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <REDACTED>' } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('evt', e.data);
es.onerror = () => { /* reconnect logic reads lastEventId */ }
```

and this curl they used for server-side repro: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large \\
  -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

when they cancel the client or their proxy times out, our logs show the connection closed mid-chunk. when client reconnects using the last-event-id header we emit the next events but the previously-sent final chunk is missing a trailing brace and there is no explicit termination event — so the consumer never gets finish_reason or the final object.

sam-ops: interesting — got a snippet of their edge logs from our access logs: 
```
[edge] 2025-10-05T16:12:33Z conn=abcd1234 recv=chunk(512) -> client disconnected (RST)
[edge] 2025-10-05T16:12:33Z stream aborted, req_id=req-789
```

looks like the upstream runtime flushed some frames but the socket closed before the final flush. likely a timeout on their proxy. do we treat partial frames as committed?

maria-engineer: our runtime writes SSE events like: 
```
data: {"token":"...","text":"..."}\n\nid: 12345\n
```
and at completion we send: 
```
data: {"finish_reason":"stop","token":""}\n\nid: 12345\n
```
If the connection drops before that final completion event, the client will have an incomplete JSON blob unless the client assembles only on newline-complete boundaries. if they reconnect with last-event-id and we re-emit starting at the next id, the partial last fragment is lost from their local state.

julia-docs: action items for support: clarify to customer that short-term workaround is to buffer only fully-terminated JSON objects on client side (wait for closing brace + optional finish_reason field) and on reconnect request a fresh response rather than relying on the last partial event. but we should fix server-side to avoid leaving dangling partial events.

sam-ops: also check if any of our proxies (nginx/ELB/Cloudflare) are enabling response buffering or idle timeouts. common culprits: nginx proxy_read_timeout (default 60s), ALB idle timeout, corporate proxies that do early-close. if proxy does internal buffering we might deliver in larger chunks and on close mid-buffer the client sees truncated JSON.

alex.support: customer says they see this infrequently (1-2%), but it's enough to break downstream parsers that expect complete JSON per event. they provided a sample captured event: 
```
data: {"id": "tok_9f", "text":"... continues ...", "meta": {...}\n\n```
(note missing trailing brace and missing finish_reason).

maria-engineer: proposed runtime fixes: 
- always emit a small newline-terminated keepalive event at fixed intervals (we already do, but make it flush after each write)
- ensure each SSE event body is self-contained and either contains a full JSON envelope or an explicit partial flag so clients know to re-assemble.
- on reconnection with Last-Event-ID, if server detects a likely previous abrupt close for that stream id, emit an explicit "stream-resume" event that signals clients to re-request or to drop any cached partial buffer.

repro-bot: created ticket RNW-3421 and added runtime/edge teams. priority P2.

sam-ops: in the short term we can advise customers: 
- prefer server-side clients that re-request full response instead of piecing partial events on Last-Event-ID.
- implement a small local reassembly window: keep last 2 events buffer, treat any event missing a finish_reason or closing brace as invalid after reconnect.
- set their proxy keepalive > 120s or disable intermediate buffering for stream endpoints.

julia-docs: doc update item: add "handling truncated SSE events" section showing a robust client strategy (example node fetch + streaming parse with JSON.parse on "}\n\nmaria-engineer: technical note for runtime: we need to make finalization idempotent and ensure that if a stream aborted mid-event we either (A) re-send the full last event on resume, or (B) emit an explicit terminal event that allows client to know previous event is incomplete. I'll follow up on RNW-3421 with a proposed patch.

alex.support: forwarding this thread to the customer with the workaround and RNW-3421 reference. i'll ping once we have a patch or hotfix. :thumbsup:
